question: What is the very first step in how cancer starts in the body?

options.C: Rapid spread of bacteria in the blood
options.D: Genetic mutation in a single cell

explanation: Cancer kicks off when a change happens in a cell's genes, making it grow and divide without stopping. You've got this! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is the nurse's role so important when a patient is first told they might have cancer?

options.A: To determine the final pathological tumor grade
options.B: To perform surgical removal of the tumor mass
options.C: To prescribe and administer initial chemotherapy doses
options.D: To reduce anxiety and guide patients through complex tests

explanation: Finding out about cancer is super scary. Nurses step in as guides and educators to help patients understand tests and calm their fears. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which special scan uses a tiny, safe radioactive substance to check for active changes in body tissues?
explanation: A PET scan uses a special tracer to light up how tissues and organs are working on a cellular level. Pretty neat technology! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h2)

question: A healthy 50-year-old woman asks why she needs a routine mammogram when she feels fine. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Routine screening is legally required for all women over the age of forty in this country.
options.B: Screening tests catch cancer early before symptoms develop, which makes treatment more successful.
options.C: These tests are designed to prevent normal cells from ever mutating into cancerous growths.
options.D: Mammograms are only performed after a physician feels a distinct lump during a physical exam.

explanation: Screening is all about catching things early before they turn into bigger problems. Early detection makes treatment much easier! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h2)

question: What does tumor 'staging' mainly tell the healthcare team?

options.A: The exact microscopic appearance and shape of the cells
options.B: The size of the tumor and how far it has spread
options.C: The speed at which the patient's hair falls out
options.D: The specific type of chemotherapy needed for cure

explanation: Staging helps doctors figure out how big the tumor is and if it has traveled to other parts of the body. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h3)

question: How do high-grade cancer cells usually act compared to low-grade cancer cells?

options.A: High-grade cells never metastasize to lymph nodes.
options.B: High-grade cells are easier to destroy with basic antibiotics.
options.C: High-grade cells look identical to healthy tissue under a lens.
options.D: High-grade cells grow and spread much more rapidly.

explanation: High-grade cells are fast-growing and more aggressive, meaning doctors need to act quickly. You're doing great learning this! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why is a biopsy a must-have test when checking for cancer?

options.A: It replaces the need for laboratory blood testing entirely.
options.B: It lowers systemic blood pressure during diagnostic scans.
options.C: It completely cures the patient by removing all toxins.
options.D: It provides definitive microscopic proof of malignancy.

explanation: Looking at actual cells under a microscope is the only way to be 100% sure whether cancer cells are present. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the nurse's main job right after a tissue sample (biopsy) is taken?

options.A: Place the tissue sample in a household refrigerator until the morning shift
options.B: Examine the cells under the ward microscope to give an early report
options.C: Wash the specimen with sterile water to remove any residual blood
options.D: Ensure correct labeling and prompt placement in the proper preservative solution

explanation: Good lab results start with proper handling! Labeling it right away and putting it in the right preservative keeps the sample safe for testing. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the most important nursing check right after a patient has a liver biopsy?

options.A: Remove all intravenous access lines right away
options.B: Monitor vital signs and check the puncture site for bleeding
options.C: Feed the patient a large high-fiber meal immediately
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk briskly around the hospital ward

explanation: Since the liver has a huge blood supply, watching closely for bleeding and checking vital signs is top priority after this procedure. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h5)

question: A patient scheduled for a procedure with mild sedation asks for a glass of water an hour beforehand. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Explain that fasting guidelines must be followed to prevent aspiration during sedation.
options.B: Ignore the question because fluid intake does not affect anesthesia safety.
options.C: Tell the patient to drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated before the test.
options.D: Allow the patient to drink a small cup of water since it is just a liquid.

explanation: Fasting (NPO) keeps the stomach empty so the patient doesn't accidentally choke or inhale stomach contents while sedated. Safety first! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h5)

question: How should a nurse respond when a patient is extremely scared while waiting for biopsy results?

options.A: Tell them not to worry because most lumps turn out to be harmless
options.B: Remind them that other patients have much worse conditions
options.C: Change the subject immediately to cheer them up
options.D: Acknowledge their feelings and listen attentively to their concerns

explanation: Just being there, listening, and validating their worries can be a huge comfort to a terrified patient. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is a very normal emotional reaction for patients waiting to find out if they have cancer?
explanation: Waiting for big health news is terrifying. Shock and heavy anxiety are very common reactions that nurses need to be ready to support. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which medical expert spends their day looking at tissue samples under a microscope to diagnose cancer?
explanation: Pathologists are the lab detectives who study cells and tissues to give us a clear diagnosis. Teamwork makes the dream work! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why do healthcare workers use a team approach (doctors, nurses, pharmacists, etc.) in cancer care?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any nursing involvement in patient education.
options.B: It reduces hospital costs by avoiding diagnostic imaging tests.
options.C: It combines various specialties to ensure accurate diagnosis and comprehensive treatment planning.
options.D: It allows a single doctor to make all clinical decisions without consulting others.

explanation: Cancer care is complex! Working together ensures that every single physical, emotional, and medical need of the patient is met. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h7)
